sentences.text: A cloud is not made of cotton, smoke, or soft stone.
It is made of tiny water droplets or tiny bits of ice.
Water can float in the air as a gas called water vapor, and vapor is invisible.
When the air cools, that vapor turns into droplets around specks of dust.
The droplets are so small and light that they can stay up.
A puffy white cloud on a fair day is often called a cumulus cloud.
A flat gray sheet of cloud is often called stratus.
A gray cloud is usually thicker, so less sunlight gets through.
If the droplets join together and grow heavy, they can fall as rain.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: What clouds are made of and how they form
How to paint a cloud with cotton
Why dust never leaves the ground

questions.explanation: The passage explains that clouds are droplets or ice, tells how vapor cools into droplets, and names two cloud shapes. That is the main idea.

questions.prompt: Water vapor in this passage is what?

choices.text: A flat gray sheet of cloud

questions.explanation: The passage says water can float in the air as a gas called water vapor, and that vapor is invisible. The definition is right there.

questions.prompt: What is a flat gray sheet of cloud often called?
questions.explanation: The passage says a puffy white cloud is often cumulus, and a flat gray sheet is often stratus. The shape in the question matches stratus.
